conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know a bit about the child or children you're claiming for.

**First question: How old is your child?**

The eligibility rules vary depending on age:
- Children under 16 may automatically qualify
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over are not eligible

Please tell me your child's age, and if you have multiple children, let me know their ages as well.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have three children - Alex is 7, Blake is 12, and Charlie is 10.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have three children:
- **Alex** (age 7)
- **Blake** (age 12)
- **Charlie** (age 10)

All three of your children are under 16, which is good news as they fall into the automatic qualification age category. However, I need to check a few more things to determine eligibility.

Let me ask you about each child. **For children under 16, they must not be working full-time (16 hours or more per week).**

**Are any of your children (Alex, Blake, or Charlie) working 16 hours or more per week?**

This would be unusual for children of their ages, but I need to confirm this requirement.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of them work at all. They're just regular school kids.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Since Alex (7), Blake (12), and Charlie (10) are all under 16 and not working full-time, they all meet the basic child qualifications.

Now I need to check your eligibility as the claimant. Let me move to the next set of questions.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are any of your children receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

This would include benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit that are claimed in the child's own name (not as part of your household claim).

For children aged 7, 10, and 12 attending regular school, this would be very unusual, but I need to confirm - are any of them receiving these types of benefits in their own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of them get any benefits themselves. They're just kids.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue checking the requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are any of your children in an apprenticeship program?**

Again, for children aged 7, 10, and 12 in regular school, this would be very unlikely, but I need to confirm they are not in any apprenticeship programs.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they're not in any apprenticeships. They're still in primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now that we've confirmed all three children qualify, let me check your eligibility as the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your residency status. Do you meet UK residency requirements?**

You qualify if ANY of the following apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (most common)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3+ months)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (for up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support your family (and not claiming certain benefits)
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Do any of these apply to you?** The most straightforward is if you normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. You're living abroad at the moment. Let me check if you might still qualify under special circumstances.

**Are you living abroad as a Crown servant?** This includes:
- Civil servants working for the UK government
- Members of HM Forces
- Similar positions serving the Crown overseas

Or **are you living in certain qualifying countries** that have special agreements with the UK?

If neither of these apply, could you tell me:
- How long have you been living abroad?
- Do you have any connection to the UK (such as UK citizenship, previous UK residence, etc.)?

This will help me determine if there are any other pathways that might apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I'm just living abroad as a regular person.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Based on what you've told me, I need to proceed with the assessment based on the residency requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for UK Child Benefit** for Alex, Blake, and Charlie.

**Reason:** You do not meet the UK residency requirements.

**Why this matters:** To claim Child Benefit, you must either:
- Normally live in the UK, OR
- Meet special circumstances such as:
  - Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with additional qualifying criteria)
  - Being a Crown servant living abroad
  - Living in certain qualifying countries with special agreements

Since you're living abroad as a regular person and don't meet any of the special circumstances, you unfortunately don't qualify for Child Benefit.

**What this means:** Even though your three children (Alex, Blake, and Charlie) all meet the child qualification requirements, the claimant (you) must also meet the residency requirements to receive the benefit.

**Possible next steps:**
- If you move back to the UK and normally reside there, you would be able to claim Child Benefit at that time
- If your circumstances change (e.g., you become a Crown servant), you may become eligible

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify about these requirements?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. So even though my kids would qualify, I can't claim it because I'm not living in the UK myself. That makes sense, I suppose. Thank you for explaining that to me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're exactly right - you've understood it perfectly. Your children Alex (7), Blake (12), and Charlie (10) all meet the child qualification requirements, but the claimant (you) must also meet the UK residency requirements for the claim to be successful.

Let me now record the formal eligibility outcome for your situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you. 

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you move back to the UK - you would be able to claim Child Benefit at that time for your children. The good news is that your children clearly meet all the necessary requirements, so it would just be a matter of your residency status.

If you have any other questions about benefits or if you'd like information about what might happen if you return to the UK, feel free to ask. Best of luck to you and your family!
